1. Outside view. The series has been hovering in the low 50s throughout July and early August (reaching a low of 50). This is typical for Google Trends search interest for "iPhone" during the mid-summer lull. Historically, the search interest forms a U-shape between iPhone cycles, peaking at 100 during the September release week, declining over the winter and spring (with spikes at Black Friday/Christmas and the June WWDC event, which brought it to 64-69 this year), and bottoming out in July before climbing again in late August as rumors and official event announcements circulate. A naive extrapolation of recent weeks would predict 52-56.

2. Inside view. The target week is Sunday, August 23 to Saturday, August 29, 2026. This specific week is highly critical in Apple's typical calendar. Since Labor Day in 2026 falls on Monday, September 7, Apple is overwhelmingly likely to hold its iPhone event on either Tuesday, September 8 or Wednesday, September 9. Following their reliable historical pattern, media invitations for a September 8-9 event would be sent out exactly two weeks prior—most likely on Tuesday, August 25 or Wednesday, August 26. This official announcement will fall precisely in the middle of the target week, triggering a wave of mainstream tech coverage and a noticeable, but not peak, spike in "iPhone" search interest. This specific catalyst should lift the index meaningfully above the summer baseline, likely up to the high 50s or low 60s, though still well short of WWDC levels or the actual launch peak. We will assign an upward adjustment of about +4 to +8 points from the baseline.

3. Pre-mortem. If this forecast is wrong, the most likely cause is a mismatch in timing. If Apple decides to hold their event in the third week of September (e.g., September 15) and delays sending invitations until September 1, the target week of August 23-29 would miss the announcement spike, and the index could languish around 53-55. Alternatively, a major leak from a prominent analyst could drive the index higher into the mid-to-high 60s. We will widen the standard deviation to cover both the possibility of a delayed announcement (lower bound) and heavy rumors (upper bound).

4. Calibrate. Given a recent baseline around 52-56 and an expected invitation-bump up to around 58-62, a mean of 59 with an SD of 4.5 comfortably captures the probable outcomes (approx 54.5 to 63.5), accounting for both a quiet week and a noisy rumor cycle.
